title: Comparison of Balance Changes After Inspiratory Muscle or Otago Exercise Training
author: Francesco Ferraro
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8vhhw36
materials: Maximal Static Respiratory Muscle Function. A hand-held mouth pressure meter MicroRPM (Micro Medical Ltd, Rochester, Kent, UK) was used for the determination of maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) during a quasi-static effort (i.e. Mueller manoeuvre), in conjunction with Micro Medical PUMA software (Micro Medical Ltd, Rochester, Kent, UK) for recording the measurements. The pressure meter incorporates a small air vent, which prevents the production of artificially high pressures generated by the muscles of the buccal cavity when the glottis is closed. The vent was small enough (~1 cm) that it did not significantly affect lung volumes during maximum efforts. Participants breathed via a flanged mouthpiece while wearing a nose-clip. The device was capable of measuring differential pressure between 300 cmH 2 O. Since MIP measurements are dependent on lung volume, each effort was initiated from residual volume or total lung capacity, respectively. The test manoeuvre consisted of isolated concentric muscle contractions to avoid the variability that is caused by the stretch-shortening cycle of the respiratory muscles. All manoeuvres were sustained for 3 to 4 seconds while seated, and participants were instructed to exert efforts rapidly and maximally. In addition, participants were provided with strong verbal encouragement in support: “ Breathe in hard - pull, pull, pull ”; Before testing, all participants practised the Müller manoeuvres three times, and measurements were repeated at least five, but no more than eight times, until variability was < 10% in three consecutive manoeuvres, from which the best was recorded. The required time to administer the test was between 10 and 15 minutes. The effects of 8 weeks of inspiratory muscle training on the balance of healthy older adults: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.. Physiological reports. Peak Inspiratory Muscle Power (PIP). Using the POWERbreathe ® K5 with Breathe-Link 2.0 software participants inhaled with maximal effort against six discrete load settings: 40%, 50%, 55%, 60%, 70% and 80% of their [baseline] MIP. Three trials were performed for each of the loading intensities with 30 seconds rest intervals between efforts, for a total of 18 maximal inspiratory manoeuvres. All loads were assigned randomly using free software available on randomizer.org. All manoeuvres were performed seated, wearing the nose-clip and within a 20 minutes period. Participants received visual feedback of pressure from the Breathe-Link 2.0 software to prepare them for the magnitude of the ensuing inspiratory efforts and were instructed to inhale with maximal effort as rapidly as possible. The assessment of maximal respiratory mouth pressures in adults.. Respiratory care. Measurement validity of an electronic inspiratory loading device during a loaded breathing task in patients with COPD.. Respiratory medicine.

steps.title: Prepare Participants and Environment
steps.instruction: Standardize the testing environment and ensure participants are prepared according to study requirements.

substeps.instruction: Set laboratory temperature to 20-22 °C and humidity to < 70%.
Schedule sessions between 8:00 and 11:00 am.
Ensure participants avoid alcohol, caffeinated beverages, and substances affecting physiological functions on test days.
Require participants to wear a tracksuit or shorts and t-shirts, with plimsolls or trainers.
Obtain written informed consent and familiarize participants with procedures via verbal explanation and information sheets.

steps.title: Collect Demographic and Physical Data
steps.instruction: Measure the participant's stature and body mass.

substeps.instruction: Measure free-standing stature to the nearest 0.1 cm using a stadiometer (SECA 217); participants must stand barefoot, heels together, arms at sides, buttocks and scapulae in contact with the device, looking straight ahead and taking a deep breath.
Record body mass in minimal clothing using an electronic weighing scale (Mc 780 MA, Tanita Body Composition Analyser).

steps.title: Perform Health and Cognitive Screening
steps.instruction: Administer questionnaires to screen for exclusion criteria and cognitive/functional status.

substeps.instruction: Complete health check questionnaires to exclude participants with falls in the past two years, heart conditions preventing activity, beta-blocker use, vertigo in the past six months, or diabetes.
Administer the Activities-Specific Balance Confidence (ABC) Scale (16 items, 0-100% scale) over 5-10 minutes.
Administer the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) 2.0 (10 items, 0-5 score).
Administer the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE); only participants with a total score ≥ 25 (absence of cognitive impairment) are recruited. Administration takes 5-10 minutes.

steps.title: Conduct Respiratory Function Tests
steps.instruction: Measure lung capacity and inspiratory flow rate using a spirometer and electronic loading device.

substeps.instruction: Measure Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) and Forced Expiratory Volume (FEV1) using a hand-held spirometer (SpiroUSB, Care Fusion) with participants seated and wearing a nose clip.
Perform forced breathing manoeuvres 5-8 times until variability is within 5% in three consecutive manoeuvres; use the highest score.
Allow 1-2 minutes of rest between measurements.
Calculate the Tiffeneau-Pinelli index (FEV1/FVC); only participants with a ratio > 0.7 are included.
Measure Peak Inspiratory Flow Rate (PIFR) using Powerbreathe K5 and Breathe-Link 2.0 software with participants seated and wearing a nose clip.
Instruct participants to perform 15-30 maximal inspirations (fast and deep) from complete exhalation, with 30 seconds rest between each.
Repeat until three values differ by no more than 0.10 l s-1.

steps.title: Evaluate Balance via mini-BEST
steps.instruction: Administer the mini-Balance Evaluation Systems Test (mini-BEST) to assess balance across four domains.

substeps.instruction: Perform the 14 items of the mini-BEST (anticipatory postural adjustments, postural responses, sensory orientation, and stability in gait).
Score each task from 0 (unable) to 2 (without difficulties) for a maximum total of 28 points.

steps.title: Perform 30-Second Sit to Stand Test
steps.instruction: Count the number of sit-to-stand transitions completed in 30 seconds.

substeps.instruction: Use a standard armless chair with a 46 cm seat height, placed next to a wall for safety.
Position participant sitting at the chair edge, hips in neutral abduction/rotation, not touching the seatback, with arms across the chest and blindfolded.
After 15 seconds of usual sitting, command '3, 2, 1 and go' to start the 30-second timer.
Participant must rise and sit as fast as possible with full range of motion, keeping both feet on the floor.

steps.title: Perform Pre-activation 30sSTS (30sSTS PA)
steps.instruction: Assess the effect of acute inspiratory muscle activation on the 30sSTS task.

substeps.instruction: Provide a 2-5 minute rest interval after the initial 30sSTS.
Perform 30 repetitions of forceful inhalations against a load of 50% of baseline MIP.
Perform forceful inhalations at 80% of baseline MIP until repetition failure (provide verbal encouragement).
Stop forced inspiration after three consecutive failed attempts and immediately perform the 30sSTS PA.

steps.title: Conduct Timed Up and Go (TUG) Variants
steps.instruction: Measure the time to complete a stand-walk-turn-sit sequence under three different conditions.

substeps.instruction: Standard TUG: From a 46 cm armless chair, stand up, walk 3 meters, turn around a cone, walk back, and sit down. Record time in seconds.
Cognitive TUG (TUG C): Perform the TUG while counting down backwards in threes from a random number (80-100) provided immediately before the start.
Motor TUG (TUG M): Perform the TUG while holding a 70 cm wide tray with a glass (8 cm diameter, 9.5 cm height) filled with water (1 cm from the top).
Ensure participants do not know the results of any TUG variant until all three are completed.

steps.title: Perform Isometric Sit-Up Test
steps.instruction: Assess anterior trunk muscle endurance using an isometric sit-up.

substeps.instruction: Position participant on an examination bench with the upper body against a support at a 60° angle.
Flex knees and hips to 90°, fold arms across the chest, and secure feet with straps.
At the command '3, 2, 1 and go', pull the support back approximately 10 cm.
Record the time until the participant experiences discomfort or can no longer hold the position.

steps.title: Perform Biering-Sørensen Test
steps.instruction: Assess posterior trunk muscle endurance in a prone position.

substeps.instruction: Position participant prone on an examination table with the iliac crest on the edge.
Secure the lower body with two straps around the pelvis and knees; the investigator holds the ankles.
Instruct participant to lift the upper body with arms behind the head, maintaining neutral trunk alignment.
Record the time until the participant experiences discomfort or the trunk deviates > 10° from neutral alignment.
